Mike Waltz, U.S. ambassador to the United Nations, honored fallen American troops on Tuesday by leading service members in a pushup session.

Waltz, alongside a video shared to his X account, wrote — while misspelling Beirut — that he was “knocking out 20 with the Marines guarding Embassy Beruit in honor of the 241 Americans murdered by Iran & Hezbollah in 1983. Oorah! Semper Fi. 👊🇺🇸.”

The clip shows Waltz — a U.S. Army Special Forces veteran — wearing a suit and dropping down to the ground in front of a line of 10 service members who follow his lead as someone calls for pushups. The video ends as the group comes around to its 11th pushup.

Critics put Waltz on blast over his pushup tribute, including an X user who wrote, “Even the most viscious ISIS combatant couldn’t come up with something as cruel as equating 1 pushup to approximately 12 American lives.”

Others slammed the move, with one writing that the last thing they’d want as a Marine would be for “some suit” to make them do pushups for “his social media clout” and another who claimed Waltz didn’t do the pushups to “honor” anyone.

“It’s this kind of insecure, performative horse shit…that rips the seriousness out of anything these people say. Mike wanted a video to post so he could look like a ‘stud.’ Instead…he looked stupid,” wrote podcaster Jack Hopkins.

And Mouin Rabbani, a Middle East analyst, teased, “If this doesn’t stop Iran from deploying dirty bombs in every major US city and end the Islamic Republic, nothing will.”
